verdicts.claim: PASSIVE mode copies as many frames as possible without waiting for readers or writers, so it may leave the checkpoint unfinished
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'Checkpoint as many frames as possible without waiting for any database readers or writers to finish ... passive mode might leave the checkpoint unfinished if there are concurrent readers or writers.'

verdicts.claim: FULL waits until there is no writer and readers use the newest snapshot, then copies all WAL frames; it blocks new writers while pending
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'blocks ... until there is no database writer and all readers are reading from the most recent database snapshot. It then checkpoints all frames ... blocks new database writers while it is pending'

verdicts.claim: RESTART adds a wait until readers no longer need the WAL
verdicts.evidence: pragma: 'works the same way as FULL with the addition that after checkpointing the log file it blocks ... until all readers are finished with the log file.'

verdicts.claim: TRUNCATE adds truncation to zero bytes after successful completion
verdicts.evidence: pragma: 'the WAL file is truncated to zero bytes upon successful completion.'

verdicts.claim: SQLite's documented default automatic-checkpoint threshold is 1000 WAL pages; triggered by a commit that brings the WAL to that size or larger
verdicts.evidence: wal.html §3.1: 'automatically checkpoint whenever a COMMIT occurs that causes the WAL file to be 1000 pages or more in size'

verdicts.claim: Applications can change or disable the threshold
verdicts.evidence: pragma: 'Setting the auto-checkpoint size to zero or a negative value turns auto-checkpointing off.'

verdicts.claim: A successful checkpoint usually recycles the WAL for overwriting instead of shrinking the file
verdicts.evidence: wal.html §6: 'The checkpoint does not normally truncate the WAL file ... it merely causes SQLite to start overwriting the WAL file from the beginning.'

verdicts.claim: If overlapping read transactions continuously retain older WAL snapshots, checkpoints may be unable to complete and reset the WAL, allowing growth
verdicts.evidence: wal.html §6: 'if ... there is always at least one active reader, then no checkpoints will be able to complete and hence the WAL file will grow without bound.'

verdicts.claim: Litestream broadly says checkpointing can only happen when no transactions are active
verdicts.evidence: litestream: checkpointing 'can only be done when no transactions are active.'
